OpenObserve keeps recent data in memory, so it is stopped while its folder is copied (seconds to minutes, depending on its size); the collector keeps retrying what arrives meanwhile for up to five minutes. It holds secrets. External databases are left out; `app backup` saves the apps' data on them.

`server restore` is for a server that doesn't have these shared apps yet (exit 3 if one is deployed). It puts back the records and files, deploys the shared apps, loads their data and then deploys Keycloak, which finds its data in the restored database, and OpenObserve, which needs Caddy for its domain. The `monitoring` of shared apps is set up in that last step too.

## Moving to a new server

```sh
compost server backup -o old.compost.tar.gz -s old
compost app backup --all --include sources,volumes,images -o apps.compost.tar.gz -s old

compost server define new --address 198.51.100.7
compost server restore old.compost.tar.gz -s new --yes
compost app restore apps.compost.tar.gz --all -s new --yes
```

The server dump already holds the apps' databases and their link records keep the same credentials, so restore apps without `links`. Point DNS to the new server; Caddy's certificates came along, so there's no wait for Let's Encrypt.

---

<!-- Configuration.md -->

# Configuration

| File | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| [`compost.yaml`](#compostyaml) | App repository | How the app is deployed. Commit it. |
| [Overlay](#overlays), e.g. `.compost-staging.yaml` | Anywhere, or stored on the server | Values of one instance, incl. secrets |
| [`compost-server.yaml`](#compost-serveryaml) | Infrastructure folder | The server's shared apps. Commit it. |
| `.compost-server.secrets.yaml` | Infrastructure folder | Shared apps' secrets ([Secrets](Secrets.md#shared-apps)) |
| [`servers.yaml`](#serversyaml), [`config.yaml`](#preferences) | `~/.compost` | Your servers and preferences |

Names (apps, prefixes, shared apps, link entries) use lowercase letters, digits and `-`, start with a letter and have at most 31 characters. App names starting with `compost-` are reserved.

## How files are merged

`-f a.yaml -f b.yaml` or `-f a.yaml,b.yaml` deep-merges the files in order:

1. Maps merge key by key.
2. Lists whose items all have a `name` merge **by name**: matching items merge, new ones are appended.
3. Other lists and values from later files replace earlier ones.

So an overlay only repeats the names and the keys it changes:

```yaml
services:
  ingress:
    - name: site                      # merged into the `site` entry of compost.yaml
      domains: [staging.example.com]
```

Without `-f`: `server deploy` loads `compost-server.yaml` and `.compost-server.secrets.yaml` (if present); `app deploy` loads `compost.yaml`. The merge result plus defaults is the **effective configuration**, which is validated, shown by `--dry-run` and stored on the server without secrets.

## compost.yaml

```yaml
name: myapp                            # required
deployment:
  type: docker-compose                 # the only type
  source_dir: .                        # folder uploaded and holding the compose file; relative to compost.yaml
  compose_file: docker-compose.yaml    # default; relative to source_dir
  compose_overrides: []                # more compose files applied after it; relative to compost.yaml
  build: false                         # true: `docker compose build` on the server; false: `pull`
  attach_sources: false                # upload the whole folder; forced true by build: true
services:
  ingress: [ … ]                       # see Applications
  database: [ … ]
  oidc: [ … ]
  monitoring: [ … ]
app_services:
  - name: backend                      # name used by links
    service: backend-webapp            # service in the compose file
    environment:                       # fixed variables
      APP_MODE: production
backup:
  volumes: [uploads]                   # named volumes saved by `app backup`
  stop: [worker]                       # services stopped while volumes are copied; `true` for all
  before_backup: [ … ]                 # steps; see below
  after_backup: [ … ]
  before_restore: [ … ]
  after_restore: [ … ]
```

### `backup`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `volumes` | `[]` | Top-level `volumes:` keys of the compose file that `app backup` saves |
| `stop` | none | Compose services stopped while the volumes are copied, or `true` for all; `--stop` stops all |
| `before_backup`, `after_backup` | `[]` | Steps run before anything is saved and after it is saved |
| `before_restore`, `after_restore` | `[]` | Steps run before data is loaded into a deployed instance and after it is loaded |

Each step is `{exec: <service>, command: …}`, run in the service's running container, or `{run: <service>, command: …}`, a one-off container (`command` optional) that must exit with 0. A string `command` runs with `sh -c`; a list is the command and its arguments. See [Backup and restore](Backup-and-Restore.md#steps-around-a-backup-or-restore).

### `services.ingress[]`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | Entry name |
| `domains` | required unless `optional` | Usually in the overlay |
| `optional` | `false` | Skip the entry when no domains are given |
| `routes[].name` | required | |
| `routes[].target` | – | `app_services` name; with `port` |
| `routes[].port` | – | Container port |
| `routes[].path` | `/` | |
| `routes[].strip_prefix` | `false` | Forward `/ui/x` as `/x` |
| `routes[].link` | – | `<kind>/<entry>` of another link instead of `target`/`port`, e.g. `oidc/login` |

### `services.database[]`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | Entry name |
| `type` | required | `postgres` |
| `version` | `"*"` | Requirement on the major version, e.g. `">=16"` |
| `instance` | – | Pin a shared app by name; required for an external database |
| `targets` | `[]` | `app_services` that get the variables and the network |
| `environment` | `{}` | Variable → `db_host`, `db_port`, `db_name`, `db_user`, `db_password`, `db_url` |
| `db_name`, `db_user` | `<app>_<prefix>_<entry>` | Overlay. `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$` |
| `db_password` | generated | Overlay, secret. Required for an external database without root credentials |

### `services.oidc[]`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name`, `type` | required | `type: keycloak` |
| `version`, `instance` | `"*"`, – | As for databases |
| `realm` | `<app>-<prefix>` | Created if missing |
| `client_id` | `<app>-<prefix>-<entry>` | |
| `public_client` | `false` | No client secret |
| `public_url` | – | The realm's own domain; needs an ingress route with `link: oidc/<entry>` |
| `redirect_uris` | required | |
| `web_origins` | `[]` | |
| `client_secret` | generated | Secret |
| `users[]` | `[]` | `username`, `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `password`. Secret |
| `targets`, `environment` | | Values: `oidc_issuer`, `oidc_internal_url`, `oidc_realm`, `oidc_client_id`, `oidc_client_secret` |

### `services.monitoring[]`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | Entry name |
| `instance` | – | Pin a monitoring app by name; required when the server has several |
| `optional` | `false` | Skip the entry when the server runs no monitoring app |
| `targets` | `[]` | `app_services` whose output is collected and that get the variables and the network |
| `logs` | `true` | Collect the output of `targets`. Fails for a service with its own `logging` |
| `metrics[]` | `[]` | Prometheus endpoints: `target` (`app_services` name), `port`, `path` (default `/metrics`) |
| `environment` | `{}` | Variable → `otlp_endpoint`, `otlp_grpc_endpoint`, `otlp_protocol`, `service_name`, `resource_attributes` |

At least one of `targets` and `metrics` is required.

Details and examples: [Applications](Applications.md).

## Overlays

Same schema as `compost.yaml`, plus `prefix` (default `main`). Typically:

```yaml
prefix: staging
services:
  ingress:
    - name: site
      domains: [staging.example.com]
  database:
    - name: main-db
      db_password: …
app_services:
  - name: backend
    environment:
      APP_MODE: staging
```

An overlay stored with `secret deploy` also needs `name`. See [Secrets](Secrets.md).

## compost-server.yaml

```yaml
shared:
  ingress:
    - {name: caddy-main, type: caddy, version: 2, configuration: {…}}
  database:
    - {name: postgres18, type: postgres, version: 18, image: postgres:18-alpine}
    - {name: shop-db, type: postgres, version: 16, external: {host: db, network: shop_default}}
  oidc:
    - {name: keycloak, type: keycloak, version: 26, configuration: {url: https://auth.example.com}}
  monitoring:
    - {name: monitoring, type: openobserve, version: 1, configuration: {url: https://logs.example.com}}
backup:
  target: local                        # local | server | s3 (not implemented)
  server_path: backups                 # folder of the server target
```

Each type's keys: [Servers and shared apps](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md#shared-app-types), and [External databases](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md#external-databases) for `external`. At most one ingress per server.

Keys every shared app has:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name`, `type` | required | |
| `version` | per type | Major version |
| `image` | per type | |
| `configuration` | `{}` | The type's keys |
| `external` | – | A server compost doesn't run; databases only |
| `monitoring` | – | Send its output and metrics to a monitoring app: `instance`, `logs` (default `true`), `metrics` (default `true`). See [Monitoring shared apps](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md#monitoring-shared-apps) |

## servers.yaml

Written by `server define`; you rarely edit it.

```yaml
servers:
  - name: prod
    connector:
      type: ssh                        # ssh | local
      address: 203.0.113.10
      port: 22                         # optional
      user: compostuser                # default
      identity_file: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 # optional; default: ssh config, agent, ~/.ssh/id_*
    server_home: ~/.compost-server     # default
    deploy:
      apply: false                     # optional, see below
  - name: dev
    connector:
      type: local
```

## Preferences

```sh
compost config set deploy.apply true [--for-server prod]
compost config unset deploy.apply [--for-server prod]
compost config show
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `deploy.apply` | `false` | `server deploy` and `app deploy` start services without `--apply` |

`--apply`/`--no-apply` win over the server's value, which wins over the global one in `~/.compost/config.yaml`.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COMPOST_HOME` | compost's local folder, default `~/.compost` |
| `COMPOST_SERVER` | Target server, when `-s` isn't given (wins over the context) |

---

<!-- Files-and-Folders.md -->

# Files and folders

## On your machine

`~/.compost`, or `$COMPOST_HOME`:

```
~/.compost/
├── compost-manager.yaml    manager key; copy it (or use `init --key`) to manage the same servers elsewhere
├── servers.yaml            servers from `server define`
├── config.yaml             preferences from `compost config`
├── current_context         server name from `connect`
└── ssh/                    shared SSH connection sockets
```

## In an app repository

```
myapp/
├── docker-compose.yaml                compose file, never changed by compost
├── compost.yaml                       how to deploy; commit
├── .compost.secrets.example.yaml      example overlay from `app generate`; commit
├── .compost-staging.yaml              overlay with secrets; don't commit
├── .compostignore                     not uploaded (gitignore syntax)
├── .claude/skills/compost/            Agent Skill from `compost agent skill`, if you install it there
└── …
```

Not uploaded with the sources: `.git/`, files given with `-f`, `.compost-*.yaml`, `.compost.*.yaml` and `.compostignore` patterns. With `deployment.source_dir`, the uploaded folder is that one instead, and `compost.yaml` can live in a separate deployment repository ([Applications](Applications.md#sources-in-another-folder)).

## In an infrastructure folder

```
infra/
├── compost-server.yaml                    shared apps; commit
├── compost-server.prod.yaml               overrides for the real server; commit
├── .compost-server.secrets.example.yaml   commit
└── .compost-server.secrets.yaml           secrets; don't commit
```

## On the server

`~/.compost-server` of the server user, or `server_home` from `servers.yaml`. compost writes only here and to Docker.

```
~/.compost-server/
├── manager_key                       key of the compost installation managing this server
├── compost-server.yaml               effective server config, without secrets
├── state.yaml                        status of shared apps and instances
├── lock/                             exists while a command changes the server
├── tmp/                              short-lived files, e.g. client credentials for external databases
├── backups/                          archives of the `server` backup target
├── secrets/apps/<app>/<prefix>.yaml  overlay stored by `secret deploy`
├── shared/
│   ├── ingress/caddy-main/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── compose.override.yaml     from its `monitoring`, if set
│   │   ├── conf/Caddyfile
│   │   ├── conf/sites/<instance>-<entry>.caddy
│   │   ├── conf/custom/<site>.caddy  `sites` of compost-server.yaml
│   │   ├── data/                     certificates
│   │   └── config/
│   ├── database/postgres18/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── data/                     PGDATA
│   │   └── secrets/postgres.env      root password
│   ├── oidc/keycloak/
│   │   ├── compose.yaml
│   │   ├── compose.override.yaml     networks and database settings from its links
│   │   └── secrets/keycloak.env      admin user and password
│   └── monitoring/monitoring/
│       ├── compose.yaml              openobserve and collector
│       ├── compose.override.yaml     ingress network, if `url` is set
│       ├── data/                     OpenObserve's data
│       ├── collector/config.yaml
│       ├── collector/targets/<instance>-<entry>.yaml   metrics endpoints of a link
│       └── secrets/                  openobserve.env, collector.env: root email and password
├── connectors/                       link records, one per instance and entry
│   ├── ingress/caddy-main/<instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   ├── database/postgres18/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   │                                 (for an external database: how to reach it, and root credentials)
│   ├── oidc/keycloak/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│   └── monitoring/monitoring/root-connector.yaml, <instance>-<entry>.yaml
│                                     (root-connector.yaml: URL and root login)
└── apps/<app>/<prefix>/
    ├── sources/                      uploaded files; .compost/ holds the compose_overrides
    ├── compose/compost.override.yaml networks and variables added to your services
    ├── compost.yaml                  effective app config, without secrets
    └── compost-env.yaml              shared apps this instance uses; links still to remove
```

Files with secrets (`secrets/`, connector records of databases and OIDC, `root-connector.yaml` files, `compost.override.yaml`) have mode `0600`, their folders `0700`. Only compost writes `state.yaml`.

## Docker names

| Object | Name |
|---|---|
| Instance compose project | `<app>-<prefix>`, e.g. `myapp-staging` |
| Shared app compose project | `compost-<kind>-<name>`, e.g. `compost-database-postgres18` |
| Ingress network | `compost-ingress` |
| Database network | `compost-db-<name>`; the database's host name is `<name>` |
| OIDC network | `compost-oidc-<name>`; host name `<name>` |
| Monitoring network | `compost-monitoring-<name>`; the collector's host name is `<name>` |
| A service's name on the ingress and monitoring networks | `<app>-<prefix>-<service>`; for a shared app `compost-<kind>-<name>-<service>` |

So you can use plain Docker commands:

```sh
docker compose -p myapp-staging logs -f backend
docker compose -p compost-database-postgres18 exec postgres psql -U postgres
```

---

<!-- CLI-Reference.md -->

# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.sh from the help texts in src/cli; run `just docs` instead of editing. -->

The `--help` of every command. Guides: [Applications](Applications.md), [Servers and shared apps](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md), [Backup and restore](Backup-and-Restore.md).

Exit codes: `0` OK · `1` unexpected error · `2` invalid local config or usage · `3` server not ready or a server-side check failed · `4` deployed, but not healthy · `130` interrupted with Ctrl-C.

## `compost`

```text
Manage docker-based server deployments

Usage: compost [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init        Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key
  server      Define, inspect and deploy servers
  connect     Use <NAME> as the default server for following commands
  disconnect  Forget the default server
  app         Deploy and inspect user applications
  connector   Inspect links between applications and shared apps
  backup      Inspect backups
  secret      Store application secrets on the server for `app deploy`
  config      Set and show preferences, e.g. `deploy.apply`
  agent       Documentation for AI agents: llms.txt, llms-full.txt and an Agent Skill
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

## `compost init`

```text
Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key

Usage: compost init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --key <KEY>        Use this manager key (a UUID) instead of a new one, e.g. to manage the servers of another compost installation from this machine
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --force            Replace the manager key of an initialized home
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server`

```text
Define, inspect and deploy servers

Usage: compost server [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example
  define    Add or replace a server in the local configuration
  list      List defined servers
  state     Check and display server state
  deploy    Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml
  backup    Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)
  restore   Restore shared applications from a server backup
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server generate`

```text
Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example

Usage: compost server generate [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --list             List the shared app types that can be generated
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --with <WITH>      Shared app types to include, e.g. `caddy,postgres` (asked when not given)
      --force            Overwrite existing files
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server define`

```text
Add or replace a server in the local configuration

Usage: compost server define [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Server name used in other commands

Options:
      --address <ADDRESS>              Host name or IP address (SSH)
  -s, --server <SERVER>                Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --user <USER>                    SSH user [default: compostuser]
  -v, --verbose                        Print every command run on the server
      --port <PORT>                    SSH port
      --identity-file <IDENTITY_FILE>  SSH private key (default: ssh config, agent, ~/.ssh/id_*)
      --server-home <SERVER_HOME>      compost directory on the server (default ~/.compost-server)
      --local                          Manage this machine instead of a remote server
      --force                          Replace an existing server with the same name
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## `compost server deploy`

```text
Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml

Usage: compost server deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply            Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply         Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --dry-run          Validate and show what would happen without changing the server
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server backup`

```text
Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)

Usage: compost server backup [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --shared <SHARED>
          Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --format <FORMAT>
          `compost` (restorable archive) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz)
          
          [default: compost]
          [possible values: compost, raw]

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file or folder (with `--target server`: a file name in the server's backup folder)

      --target <TARGET>
          Where to write (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost server restore`

```text
Restore shared applications from a server backup

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>
          Archive written by `compost server backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --shared <SHARED>
          Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --source <SOURCE>
          Where the archive is (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost app deploy`

```text
Deploy the application instance described by the given files

Usage: compost app deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply            Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply         Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --dry-run          Validate and show what would happen without changing the server
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --purge <PURGE>    Also delete the data of links dropped from the config, for these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app state`

```text
Show the state of an application instance

Usage: compost app state [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]  Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>        Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app remove`

```text
Remove an application instance

Usage: compost app remove [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]  Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>        Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --volumes          Also remove the compose project's volumes
      --purge <PURGE>    Delete the instance's data held by these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`
      --yes              Do not ask for confirmation
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app backup`

```text
Back up an application instance (or all of them)

Usage: compost app backup [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]
          Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>
          Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --app <APP>
          Application name (instead of config files)

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)

      --all
          Back up every instance on the server into one archive

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to save (default: links,sources,volumes; only links with --link)

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --format <FORMAT>
          `compost` (restorable archive) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz)
          
          [default: compost]
          [possible values: compost, raw]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file or folder (with `--target server`: a file name in the server's backup folder)

      --target <TARGET>
          Where to write (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --stop
          Stop every service while volumes are copied, for a consistent copy (default: those in `backup.stop`)

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost app restore`

```text
Restore an application instance from a compost backup

Usage: compost app restore [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVE>

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>
          Archive written by `compost app backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
      --instance <INSTANCE>
          Instance in the archive, e.g. `myapp-staging` (needed when it has several)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: COMPOST_SERVER, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --all
          Restore every instance in the archive

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Restore under this prefix, e.g. to make a copy

  -f, --file <FILES>
          Overlays merged over the archived config, e.g. other domains (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to restore (default: all in the archive; only links with --link). Without `sources`, data is loaded into the deployed instance

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --source <SOURCE>
          Where the archive is (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --replace
          Overwrite databases and volumes that already hold data

      --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- AI-Agents.md -->

# AI agents

compost's documentation also comes in forms that AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) read well. All of them are made from these wiki pages, so they say the same, and each release carries the ones of its version.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | What compost is and a list of these pages with links, as [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) describes |
| `llms-full.txt` | Every page in one file, to give an agent the whole documentation at once |
| Agent Skill `compost` | `SKILL.md` (concepts, workflows, safety rules, which page to read for what) and these pages in `references/` |

The skill tells the agent to run `--dry-run` before deploying, and to ask you before `--apply`, removals, restores and changes to stored secrets. It never adds `--yes` on its own, and never commits or prints overlays with passwords.

## From the compost binary

The installed compost carries the files of its own version, and needs no compost home or server for them:

```sh
compost agent skill                          # writes .claude/skills/compost/ in the current folder
compost agent skill --dir ~/.claude/skills   # for all your projects
compost agent skill --dir .agents/skills     # for agents that read skills from there
compost agent llms                           # print llms.txt
compost agent llms --full                    # print llms-full.txt
```

`agent skill` replaces the `compost` skill in that folder, so run it again after updating compost. It refuses to overwrite a `compost/SKILL.md` that isn't compost's skill. You can commit the skill to your app or infrastructure repository so everyone's agent gets it.

## From a release

Every [release](https://gitrepo.dev.org.pl/dev.org.pl/compost/releases) has `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `compost-skill-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz`, listed in its `SHA256SUMS`. The archive holds the `compost` skill folder:

```sh
tar -xzf compost-skill-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz -C ~/.claude/skills
```

## From the repository

[`docs/agents`](https://gitrepo.dev.org.pl/dev.org.pl/compost/src/branch/master/docs/agents) holds the same files for master, which may describe features not released yet. An agent can fetch [`llms.txt`](https://gitrepo.dev.org.pl/dev.org.pl/compost/raw/branch/master/docs/agents/llms.txt) or [`llms-full.txt`](https://gitrepo.dev.org.pl/dev.org.pl/compost/raw/branch/master/docs/agents/llms-full.txt) from there.
